title: Cameroon's Kribi Port: 555,398 Containers, Up 82%, as Douala Waits Up to 9 Days | The Six, Ep. 24
lede: Kribi, Cameroon's deep-water port, handled 555,398 TEU in 2025, up 82.4%, after a second container terminal opened in May 2025. Douala still carries most of the country's trade but has faced vessel delays of up to nine days. Kribi's growth is now straining its own yard.
keyPoints: Kribi handled 555,398 TEU in 2025, up 82.4% and 37.5% of Cameroon's container traffic (Port Autonome de Kribi; EcoMatin).
Douala handles 75–85% of Cameroon's trade; Ecofin reported vessel delays there of up to nine days in 2025, against about two at Kribi.
Kribi's terminal two (715 m quay, 16 m deep) opened in May 2025; KCT is owned by AGL (30.83%), CMA CGM (29.62%), China Harbour (20.55%) and Cameroonian investors (19%) (EcoMatin).
Import dwell time at Kribi rose to 25.28 days in 2025 from 23.99, and ship productivity fell from 41 to 33 moves an hour (EcoMatin, Oct. 2026).
Customs receipts at Kribi reached 335–350 billion CFA francs in 2025, second only to Douala (Port Autonome de Kribi; EcoMatin).
